name: Khaleeji Bank
legal_name: Khaleeji Bank B.S.C. (formerly Khaleeji Commercial Bank B.S.C.; renamed 25 Jun 2023)
founded: 2004 (incorporated 24 November 2004, CR 55133; Islamic retail licence from the CBB; renamed from Khaleeji Commercial Bank on 25 June 2023, trading code KHCB changed to KHALEEJI)
ownership_summary: GFH Financial Group B.S.C. holds 82.95% of the ordinary shares (AR 2025 note 1, unchanged from 31 Dec 2024). The Bahrain Bourse shareholder list (issuer-provided, undated) shows this as KHCB Asset Company 43.73%, SICO B.S.C. (c) 25.00% and GFH directly 14.22%, all marked as GFH Financial Group, plus Royal Humanitarian Foundation 6.11%. The CEO, three directors and several 2026 senior hires come from GFH, and its group CEO chaired Khaleeji until 11 May 2025.

shareholders.holder: SICO B.S.C. (c) (shown as GFH Financial Group)
GFH Financial Group B.S.C. - total of the three GFH-marked holdings (stated in the annual report)

government_link: Not established. The controlling holder is GFH Financial Group (listed in Bahrain, Kuwait, Dubai and Abu Dhabi); the only other holder above 5% is Royal Humanitarian Foundation (6.11%, nature not described in the sources opened).
group_structure: Controlled by GFH Financial Group B.S.C. (Islamic wholesale bank, 82.95%), whose consolidated results include Khaleeji, so GFH figures must not be added to Khaleeji's (GFH is expected to be profiled as bh-gfh). Khaleeji's significant subsidiaries at 31 Dec 2025 (AR note 1): Surooh Limited (Cayman, 75.70%, 'Oryx Hills' real estate), KHCB Tier 1 Sukuk Limited (Cayman, 100%, AT1 issuance vehicle) and GFH Tower Group Limited (Cayman, 71.95%, new in 2025, head-office building). No overseas banking operations. Equity-accounted investees BD 6.95m at 30 Jun 2026.

subsidiaries.name: Surooh Limited
subsidiaries.activity: Construction and sale of properties at 'Oryx Hills'

subsidiaries.name: GFH Tower Group Limited
subsidiaries.activity: Head-office building and specialised real estate (holding 2025: first year)

footprint: Bahrain only. Head office at GFH Tower, Bahrain Financial Harbour, Manama; the bank's overview page lists branches at Bahrain Financial Harbour, Hidd, Sanad and Riffa (its own text says 'four branches' and names four locations, so the count is ambiguous). 193 employees at 31 Dec 2025 (181 Bahraini, 12 expatriate).
customer_segments: Personal/retail, Khaleeji VIP (invitation-only, HNW individuals, families and corporations), corporate and business banking (Hafeez digital platform), government-linked and pension-linked finance (Ministry of Housing products, SIO finance).
business_lines: Islamic retail and corporate banking: current, savings, Al Waffer and Mudharaba/Murabaha investment accounts; personal, home, auto, doctors' and housing-ministry finance; cards; business banking with the Hafeez platform; a sukuk and yielding investment book (BD 722m at 30 Jun 2026) and real-estate holdings; Khaleeji eTrade (Bahrain Bourse stock trading via Mubasher). The AR lists wealth management and structured investment products among its principal activities; a wealth, structured-products and placements team was only being assembled in Aug-Oct 2026.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Khaleeji is a small Bahraini Islamic retail bank (assets BD 1.79bn, 193 staff) controlled 82.95% by GFH Financial Group. Its wealth offer today is thin: an invitation-only Khaleeji VIP tier (dedicated relationship manager, preferential rates, higher card limits; 'VIP Mudharaba' was 21.7% of quasi-equity at Dec 2025), access for VIP clients with USD 2.5m investible assets to the third-party Opportunity Network deal portal, and Khaleeji eTrade for Bahrain Bourse stocks on Mubasher's platform. The Khaleeji app has no investing features. A rebuild began in 2026 under a new CEO who ran GFH Capital and was GFH's Group Chief Placement Officer: AGM Structured Products (16 Aug), Head of Strategy & Transformation (13 Aug), AGM Placements and a General Manager - Wealth Management (1 Oct 2026), several from GFH. No AUM, client-asset or user figures are disclosed (off-balance-sheet AUM is BD 1.5m of real estate), and H1 2026 profit fell to BD 0.4m after a Q1 loss and higher impairments.

segments.name: Khaleeji VIP
segments.eligibility: By invitation, 'limited and offered to pre-selected clients'; no minimum balance published. Benefits: dedicated relationship manager, competitive and special exchange rates, higher debit-card limits.

segments.name: Opportunity Network access (VIP)
segments.eligibility: VIP clients with minimum investible assets of USD 2.5m (corporate clients: revenue of USD 2.5m); subject to bank approval.

segments.name: Personal banking
segments.eligibility: Retail accounts including Al Waffer, Al Waffer+, salary, Ajyal and Mudharaba accounts; no wealth tier below VIP found.

private_banking.detail: Khaleeji VIP is described as premium banking for HNW individuals, families and corporations, but no investment or wealth products are listed on the page and no private-banking unit is named. A General Manager - Wealth Management took office on 1 Oct 2026.

asset_management.detail: No asset-management entity or fund range found at Khaleeji; investment arms sit in the parent (GFH Capital, GFH Partners). Off-balance-sheet AUM is BD 1.5m of real estate only.

brokerage.detail: Khaleeji eTrade: online trading of any Bahrain Bourse-listed stocks, 'powered by Mubasher Financial Services and endorsed by the Bahrain Bourse'; the account is opened through the online portal and a branch visit. Launch date, fees and minimums are not stated.

digital_investing.detail: Web-based eTrade for Bahrain Bourse stocks (Chrome-based portal, S12). The Khaleeji mobile app (iOS/Android) offers account opening, cards, bills, transfers and the 'Khaleeji 360' open-banking service but no investing features (S14).

advisory.detail: No advisory proposition found on the VIP page or elsewhere; the wealth GM role is new (Oct 2026).

discretionary.detail: No discretionary or managed-portfolio service found.

funds_platform.detail: No third-party fund shelf or platform found.

structured_products.detail: The AR lists 'structured investment products' among principal activities (note 1) and an AGM - Structured Products was appointed on 16 Aug 2026; no product page, issuer or volume found.

private_markets.detail: Only the third-party Opportunity Network deal-sharing portal for VIP and corporate clients; a Head of Placements joined in 2026 from GFH, whose group has a placement business, but no private-markets product is described.

islamic_wealth.detail: Fully Shariah-compliant bank: Al Waffer and Mudharaba/Murabaha investment accounts and VIP Mudharaba; Shari'a Supervisory Board (chair Dr Fareed Al Muftah per Bourse list). No Shariah funds or sukuk distribution found.

FY2025 results approved: attributable profit BD 11.58m (+10.27%), total income BD 63.9m (+27.9%), 6 fils cash dividend recommended; CEO calls digital transformation a main driver.
CEO Sattam Algosaibi's resignation announced (last working day 31 Mar 2026).
CFO Abdulkarim Al Zakari becomes Acting CEO.
Razi Al Murbati named CEO effective 17 Aug 2026 (corrective announcement; he remains a Board member).
H1 2026 results approved: profit attributable BD 0.4m vs BD 5.6m in H1 2025; Q1 2026 loss BD 2.4m, Q2 profit BD 2.8m.
Haifa Sulaiman Hasan (ex-GFH Capital) becomes Head of Strategy & Transformation.
Sidharth Dubey becomes AGM - Structured Products.
Ahmed Ali Salem becomes General Manager - Wealth Management.

opportunities: A wealth team was built in Aug-Oct 2026 (GM Wealth Management, AGM Structured Products, AGM Placements, Head of Strategy & Transformation) with no evidenced funds shelf, advisory, discretionary or robo offer yet (S9, S20, S22).
Khaleeji's only investing channel is a Chrome-based Bahrain Bourse trading portal on Mubasher; the mobile app has no investing features (S12, S14).
CEO Razi Al Murbati comes from GFH Capital and GFH's placement business, and the AR says principal activities include wealth management and structured investment products (S7, S9).

VIP Mudharaba was 21.7% of quasi-equity contracts at 31 Dec 2025, a VIP book large enough to need an investment proposition; VIP clients with USD 2.5m investible assets are offered a third-party deal network (S7, S13).
FY2025 release names digital transformation, deposit-base strengthening and revenue quality as strategy (S26).
barriers: Small balance sheet (BD 1.79bn) and 193 staff; H1 2026 profit BD 0.4m after a Q1 loss and BD 6.7m impairments (S3, S5, S7).
Leadership turnover: CEO resigned 31 Mar 2026, acting CEO until the new CEO's start on 17 Aug 2026, and four new heads in 2026 (S9, S17-S22).
82.95% owned by GFH, whose placement and asset-management arms are the likely product source; decisions may be taken at group level (S2, S7).
Islamic-only: product shelf must be Shariah-screened.
